methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $800M - $7.6B.

private.name: Joby Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $6.86B

data.narrative:
Archer Aviation, a public-stage drone and autonomous systems company, commands a current market valuation of $3.33B following $1.5B+ in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of four same-sector comparables spanning Series B through public stages: Zipline ($7.6B), Joby Aviation ($6.9B), Nuro ($6.0B), and Elroy Air ($800M).

A peer-median triangulation method was applied across these four firms, yielding a median implied valuation of $6.4B with a range spanning $800M to $7.6B. This method represents the sole quantitative approach applicable given current data availability. The peer set captures both earlier-stage (Elroy Air, Series B) and late-stage capital structures (Joby, public) within the Drones & Autonomous sector, providing cross-stage comparability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5B to $7.4B centered on the peer median of $6.4B. This implies a gap of approximately $3.1B between Archer's current $3.33B public valuation and the peer-derived median. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency and path-to-revenue divergence across the peer set—the four-firm sample reflects substantial stage heterogeneity, and no revenue multiples or profitability metrics are available to refine the analysis. A larger, revenue-normalized peer set would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
